acceptance: Merges no longer stall on superseded failures (sweep, docs, or rollup fix)
context: 2026-10-22 recurrence on PR #3264 (head 68de1e483): every required context had a SUCCESS instance, but two superseded failed `oracle-review` check runs (Actions runs 39706240336, synchronize; 39711741625, pull_request_review) kept the required rollup at FAILURE and mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Cancelled `gate` instances from the oracle-gate workflow's cancel-in-progress concurrency also show as failing in `gh pr checks`, though `gate` is not required. `make oracle-review-recover` could not help: it never finds failed runs (oracle-review-recover-finds-no-failed-runs-20261022). A manual `gh run rerun --failed` of both runs unblocked the merge.
description: On 2026-10-12, PRs #2822, #2829, #2830, #2875, #2876, #2878, #2905, #2908 each sat green-but-unmergable behind superseded FAILED instances in the commit rollup. Manual gh run rerun on each stale instance unblocked merge (#2829 additionally needed close+reopen for a phantom FAILURE rollup with zero failing checks). Workarounds in /tmp/benchbox-open-prs-handoff-2026-10-12.md.
